analyst_view.overall: Ipswich (16th, 11 points, three defeats in their last five, latest 2-0 at Tottenham) host Aston Villa (12th, 14 points, unbeaten in five). Villa play Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday 24 November, so they arrive with four days' rest in a run of seven games in three weeks, and they are without Onana (knee surgery, out until spring), Ruggeri and probably Matty Cash (concussion), with Wan-Bissaka also reported missing, which leaves them short at right-back and in the holding midfield role. Ipswich, under Gary O'Neil, had a fully fit squad before the Spurs trip; left-back Leif Davis rolled his ankle there but the manager hopes he is available. None of these absences is in the numbers yet, and no referee is named.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean slightly higher: Villa are without Onana, their physical shield in front of the defence, and probably both senior right-backs (Cash, Wan-Bissaka), and the numbers don't know that; a midweek trip to Istanbul adds tiredness. It is a mild lean (+3%) because Ipswich may also miss Leif Davis, their main source of crosses, so about 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already trimming Ipswich slightly for winning only 16 in their last six. If Leif Davis misses out, Ipswich lose overlapping width on the left, while a makeshift Villa right side could concede more wide entries; the two pull in opposite directions. I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, with recent card form on both sides and two past meetings already counted. No referee is named yet; a stand-in right-back facing quick wingers can draw bookings, but that is a hunch rather than news. I stay at about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, already nudging Villa up (+3%) for their recent volume. Villa's tiring schedule and missing midfield ball-winner could give Ipswich more of the ball, but Emery rotates (only 64% of his XI kept lately), which keeps legs fresh. I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. I lean slightly higher for the same reason as goals: Villa's defensive absences (Onana, Cash, Ruggeri, Wan-Bissaka) are not in the numbers and should let Ipswich into better positions. A small +3% gives about 9.3.
